title: Target Trades at a Fraction of Walmart's Valuation. Is the Discount Deserved?
detail:
Target Trades at a Fraction of Walmart's Valuation. Is the Discount Deserved?
Jeremy Bowman, The Motley Fool

Target (NYSE: TGT) and Walmart (NASDAQ: WMT) are two of the biggest retailers in the country.

As the only national, brick-and-mortar, multi-category chains where anyone can shop, the two are also close competitors, even if they have both carved out different brand identities. Over the last few years, Walmart has won that competition hands down, as the chart below shows.

TGT data by YCharts

As you can see from the chart above, Target and Walmart have gone in diametrically opposite directions, though the trend started to reverse earlier this year as Target showed some signs of life, and Walmart's comparable sales growth slowed.

While Walmart was trouncing Target, its earnings multiple got significantly higher, and at the same time, Target's fell. Foolish investors know that past performance isn't a guarantee of future returns. So is it time for a changing of the guard in big-box retail? Let's take a closer look.

Image source: Target.
Target vs. Walmart

It's understandable that Target would catch the eye of value investors at a price-to-earnings ratio of 15 and a dividend yield of 3.1%.

Additionally, under the guidance of new CEO Michael Fiddelke, the company seems to be emerging from a series of problems that challenged the retailer for years, including theft, getting dragged into culture war issues, and weak spending on discretionary items, and a slowdown coming out of a strong performance after the pandemic.

Walmart, on the other hand, now trades at a P/E ratio of 43, which reflects a consistent record of growth with comparable sales of 2% or better for every quarter for the last six years. Its investment in a network of grocery pickup stations has paid off, and it's built up its e-commerce business to a point where it's a real challenger to Amazon. That includes a Prime-like membership program, Walmart+, and it's growing its digital advertising business fast.

Which is the better buy?

Walmart deserves to have a higher earnings multiple than Target because the two are different kinds of stocks.

Walmart is one of the top, defensive, recession-proof stocks on the market, as it earns more than half of its revenue from groceries, a category people need regardless of the state of the economy.

Target, on the other hand, gets most of its revenue from discretionary goods, making it more sensitive to economic factors like inflation, which explains in part why the stock has struggled.

title: If Casey's Stock Looks Expensive, You Need To Read This

If Casey's Stock Looks Expensive, You Need To Read This

At $670.02 a share, Casey's General Stores (CASY) trades at 30.1 times adjusted earnings for the twelve months ended July 31, 2026. This metric calculates profit by adding back stock-based pay after tax. A multiple of 30.1 is steep for a convenience store chain that keeps about four cents of each sales dollar as profit, but buyers are paying for the years ahead. So what does Casey's cost on the profit forecast for fiscal 2027 and 2028?

What Casey's Stock Costs On Forecast Profit

Based on the consensus forecast, Casey's stock trades at 31.2 times expected profit for fiscal 2027 and 28.6 times expected profit for fiscal 2028. Like the 30.1 times multiple on the past twelve months, the company is priced near 30 times profit in each forecast year too. The 30.1 times figure uses adjusted earnings, and analysts' forecasts may not add back stock pay the same way. Buyers at today's price are paying in advance for the forecast profit in full.

The Profit Casey's Must Deliver For That Price

The consensus forecast for fiscal 2028 shows Casey's net income rising 9.2% on almost flat revenue, up 0.24%. Casey's delivered far faster sales growth of 13.8% over the twelve months ended July 31, 2026, so the company does not need faster sales to meet the fiscal 2028 forecast. Much of that growth came from pricier fuel: in its latest quarter, Casey's average retail fuel price rose 33%, from $3.00 to $3.99 a gallon.

That profit growth has to come from a wider margin instead. The consensus forecast projects a net margin of 4.1% for fiscal 2028, up from 3.8% for fiscal 2027. Casey's earned a 4.1% margin over the twelve months ended July 31, 2026, so the forecast asks the company to hold that level for a full fiscal year.

Casey's grew net income 27% from a year earlier in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, which ended July 31, 2026. Management said its in-store margin widened, mainly because of the mix of prepared food and dispensed beverage. Management kept its fiscal 2027 guidance for EBITDA growth at 8% to 10%. EBITDA is profit before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization. The company also said it will update its annual guidance on the second-quarter call, as it has in the past.

Where Casey's Could Miss The Forecast

Fuel margin is where Casey's is most likely to miss the consensus forecast. The chain earned a fuel margin of 47.8 cents a gallon in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, up 6.8 cents from a year earlier. Management said the fuel margin for August was in the low 40-cent range per gallon. If the fuel margin stays nearer the August level, Casey's would earn less on each gallon than it did in the first quarter. Management's fiscal 2027 EBITDA outlook, given in June, was built on a mid-40s cents-per-gallon fuel margin.

Sprouts Farmers Market Sinks 23% on Q3 Miss and Guidance Cut: "Need to Improve Our Performance" ©@PajorStudio from pixabay via Canva
Key Takeaways

Sprouts Farmers Market fell 23% today after missing third-quarter earnings estimates and forecasting a 2% to 4% drop in fourth-quarter comparable store sales.

Record store openings keep total sales growing, but transactions at existing stores fell 3.3%, and Sprouts plans to spend more on lower prices.

Walmart and Costco are still winning shoppers, while Kroger's sluggish sales suggest the soft consumer reaches traditional grocers too.

Sprouts' forward P/E was at a five-year low even before today's drop.

Sprouts Farmers Market (SFM:NASDAQ) sank 23% today after its third-quarter earnings missed estimates and its outlook got worse.

Outgoing CEO Jack Sinclair blamed "a challenging consumer environment and the cyclospora disruption," but added that "we recognize the need to improve our performance." That consumer isn't hurting everyone: Walmart (WMT:NASDAQ) and Costco (COST:NASDAQ) keep pulling in more shoppers, while Kroger (KR:NYSE) is struggling to grow sales too.

Record openings, fewer trips

Diluted EPS of $1.21 came in below the $1.23 analysts expected, and comparable store sales fell 0.9% as transactions dropped 3.3%. For the fourth quarter, Sprouts expects comps to fall 2% to 4%.

Sprouts opened a record 15 stores, and they lifted total revenue 5% to $2.30 billion, from $2.20 billion a year earlier.

Sprouts Farmers Market (SFM): total revenues, $ billions, last 8 quarters (to September 27, 2026) (TIKR)

CFO Curtis Valentine said comps softened in August and September "and did not improve as comparisons eased."

Lower prices will cost something

Sprouts now plans to spend more on affordability, including a pricing reset in January. Its gross margin had already slipped to 38.2% in the third quarter, from 38.7% a year earlier.

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Sprouts Farmers Market, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Sprouts Farmers Market's Analyst Ratings

The discounters are still winning

My read: the trips Sprouts is losing are going to the discounters. Walmart U.S. comparable sales rose 2.6% in the quarter to July 31, led by more transactions, even as Walmart ran more than 11,000 rollbacks. Its Nov. 19 report will show whether that held.

Costco's comparable sales, excluding gas and currency, grew at least 6.4% in every quarter of its fiscal year to Aug. 30. Its October sales, due in early November, are the next check.

Kroger looks more like Sprouts. Its identical sales without fuel rose just 0.2% in the quarter to Aug. 15, and it cut its full-year forecast for them to 0.2%-0.8%. Will Kroger have to match Sprouts' price cuts? Its third-quarter report, in early December, should tell us.

title: Walmart, Eli Lilly Join 38 Companies Opposing OKX-ICE Tokenized Stocks

Walmart, Eli Lilly Join 38 Companies Opposing OKX-ICE Tokenized Stocks

Walmart (NYSE: $WMT), Eli Lilly (NYSE: $LLY), Cigna Group (NYSE: $CI), Carnival (NYSE: $CCL) and Arcos Dorados (NYSE: $ARCO) have objected to plans to offer tokenized versions of their shares on a trading venue backed by crypto exchange OKX and Intercontinental Exchange (NYSE: $ICE).

The five companies were added to OKXICE TSV's list in a notice dated October 28, bringing the number of objecting companies to 38. The total has climbed from nine on October 15, as objections have spread across technology, finance, retail, health care and travel.

The latest additions include Walmart, the world's largest retailer, and Arcos Dorados, the largest McDonald's franchisee in Latin America. Both join companies that have already opposed the listings, including McDonald's (NYSE: $MCD), Microsoft (NASDAQ: $MSFT), JPMorgan Chase (NYSE: $JPM), Coca-Cola (NYSE: $KO) and Dell Technologies (NYSE: $DELL).

Eli Lilly and Cigna also add to the health care sector's representation on the list, alongside UnitedHealth Group and Moderna.

The objections have consequences under an exemption introduced by the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). Under the agency's September order, a venue seeking to offer tokenized shares issued by an unaffiliated third party must notify the company first.

If the company submits a written objection within 30 days, the venue cannot list that tokenized version of its stock under the exemption.

The rule applies to the specific trading venue, and the notices do not explain why the companies objected.

OKXICE TSV is a joint venture between ICE, the parent company of the New York Stock Exchange, and OKX's US holding company. It plans to let approved users trade tokenized US stocks around the clock through permissioned Uniswap (CRYPTO: $UNI) v4 pools on OKX's XLayer blockchain, using stablecoins such as USDC.

The list could grow further, as companies have 30 days after receiving notice to object. Major names including Nvidia (NASDAQ: $NVDA), Tesla (NASDAQ: $TSLA), Apple (NASDAQ: $AAPL) and Amazon (NASDAQ: $AMZN) have not yet objected.

Walmart, Eli Lilly, Cigna, Carnival and Arcos Dorados have joined the companies objecting to tokenized trading of their shares on OKXICE TSV, the venue that Intercontinental Exchange and OKX own together.

A public notice from the venue dated Oct. 28 lists 38 issuers under its "Notice of Issuer Objection" heading. The five companies above are the only names on it that did not appear in the Oct. 27 version, which counted 33 objectors, including JPMorgan, AMD and Coca-Cola.

As in earlier versions, the notice does not explain why any company objected. It also gives no date for when trading will start.

Get Unchained's crypto news in your inbox with the free Unchained Daily newsletter.

A List That Keeps Growing

Under the SEC exemption that allows onchain trading of tokenized stocks, a company that files a timely written objection keeps a third-party token of its stock off the venue, and the venue has to disclose the objection in an updated notice.

The Oct. 8 notice already listed four objectors, and every update since has added names. The count reached nine on Oct. 15, 16 on Oct. 19, 22 on Oct. 23 and 26 on Oct. 26 before hitting 33 on Oct. 27. Earlier objectors include Microsoft, Alphabet, Goldman Sachs, Broadcom and UnitedHealth.

How the Venue Would Work

OKXICE LLC, the Texas company behind the venue, is split 50/50 between ICE and OKC USA Holding Inc., an OKX affiliate. Trades would run through permissioned Uniswap v4 pools on X Layer, the Ethereum layer-2 network OKX launched, with access limited to wallets holding a soulbound token the venue issues. The notice says it will operate 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

The risk section is unchanged on governance. Upgrades to the venue's smart contracts need sign-off from several authorized staff. Even so, changes "take effect without a timelock, so TSV Participants may receive no advance notice of an upgrade," the notice says.

ICE and OKX formed the joint venture to bring tokenized equities to market, with former New York Gov. Andrew Cuomo as co-chair.

The world's largest retailer is now keeping its shares off OKX and ICE's planned tokenized stock venue.

Walmart, Eli Lilly, Cigna Group, Carnival, and Arcos Dorados have objected to having their shares offered on OKXICE TSV, according to an updated notice from the venue dated Wednesday. The five additions bring the total to 38 companies.

That's up from 33 a day earlier, when JPMorgan Chase, Coca-Cola and Dell were among seven newcomers. The tally has more than quadrupled since the venue's first list of nine objectors on Oct. 15. It grew to 16 on Oct. 19, with names including Microsoft, and 22 on Oct. 23 when Wells Fargo joined the list.

The latest batch broadens the pushback beyond tech and finance into retail, health care, and travel. Arcos Dorados, the largest McDonald's franchisee in Latin America, joins McDonald's itself, which objected earlier this month. Eli Lilly and Cigna join UnitedHealth Group and Moderna among the health care companies on the list.

The objections carry real weight. Under the SEC's innovation exemption, which the agency unveiled in September after the Clarity Act stalled in the Senate, a venue must notify a company before offering a version of its shares tokenized by an unaffiliated third party.

If the company objects in writing within 30 days, the venue can't make that stock available for trading, according to the SEC's order. The objection applies only to that venue, and the notices don't disclose the companies' reasons.

OKXICE TSV, a 50-50 joint venture between NYSE owner Intercontinental Exchange and OKX's U.S. holding company, plans to let approved users trade tokenized U.S. stocks around the clock. OKX and ICE first teamed up on tokenized securities earlier this year before announcing the 24/7 venue this month.

Trades would run through permissioned Uniswap v4 pools on OKX's XLayer blockchain, paired with stablecoins such as USDC. The exemption caps the venue at 75 of the largest, most liquid stocks, with trading limited to 0.25% of each stock's average daily volume, and up to 250 other stocks at 2.5%.

JPMorgan, Coca-Cola Among 7 More Companies Objecting to OKX-ICE Tokenized Stocks

The list may not be finished. Under the SEC's order, companies have 30 days from receiving notice to object, and some of the market's most heavily traded names, including Nvidia, Tesla, Apple and Amazon, haven't done so.

The venue has also said it can list shares tokenized by the issuers themselves, which would give companies direct control over how their stock appears onchain, though the notices don't identify any such listings.
